summary: Owner-run family KG (40 staff, EUR 2-5 M); our EUR 387 k is likely 8-19 % of its turnover. It has bought its 2027 steel sheet and coil forward at fixed prices (letter Oct 2026): steel moves reach its prices only from 2028. The owner prices from a two-year-old spreadsheet, offered to walk us through his calculation and calls us an important reference customer. Settles below its own ask. Sup:70360 is qualified on the coupling guard and holds 50 % of the motor bracket. Open deep; no steel increase for 2027.
notes: Steel fixed for 2027, so no material-cost basis for an increase. Wants to keep us as reference customer and its 100 % coupling-guard share; fears volume moving to Strasser (70360). We pay 9.2 days late on average without complaint. Do not cite Strasser's bracket price: it is higher (16.11 vs 15.63).

evidence.quote: he works from his own spreadsheet, last updated two years ago.
he offered to walk us through their calculation (hourly rates and material) if that helps to settle prices.
Metallbau Steinfelder KG said Hollerau is an important reference customer for them.
75.9 % of invoices paid over 5 days late
we have secured our steel sheet and coil for 2027, bought forward at fixed prices with our mill. Whatever the steel market does reaches our prices only from 2028.

arguments: its own hedge: steel fixed for 2027, no material basis for an increase
its own cost shares from the offered open-book walk-through
second source sup:70360 qualified on coupling guard: volume can move
avoid: steel-index arguments either way (its steel is fixed for 2027)
citing Strasser's bracket price (16.11, higher than its 15.63)
citing a cost driver that rose
tactics: Open deep; cite its own letter: steel is fixed for 2027, so any increase has no material basis.
Ask it to share the hourly-rate and material breakdown it offered, then argue from its own cost shares.
Point out sup:70360 is qualified on the coupling guard and could take volume.
Offer to keep it as sole source on the coupling guard in exchange for the price step.
Expect 'a fair point' and keep moving in small steps; one argument kind per round.
playbook.expected_concession: Owner-led with stale costing: history shows it settles 1.5-4 points below its own ask; no arena data.
